questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason a bank might use artificial intelligence to review thousands of loan files for compliance problems:

options.A: It replaces the bank's compliance staff
options.C: It removes the bank's legal responsibility
options.D: It guarantees every file is error-free

questions.explanation: It can flag issues quickly. AI tools can review far more files than people can in the same time and flag those that may be missing documents or breaking lending rules, so compliance staff can focus on the files most likely to have problems. The bank remains legally responsible for compliance, the AI can still miss issues or flag files incorrectly, and trained staff are still needed to make final decisions. Banks must also test these tools to make sure they don't introduce unfair bias into lending decisions.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in compliance

questions.question: A bakery sells cupcakes for $3 each. Making the 200th cupcake of the day costs an extra $1.20, but the 300th costs an extra $3.40 because staff must work overtime. Based on marginal analysis, the bakery should

options.A: cut production to 100 cupcakes.

questions.explanation: Stop before extra cost tops $3. Marginal analysis says to keep producing while the extra revenue from a unit, $3, is greater than its extra cost. The 200th cupcake adds $1.80 in profit, but the 300th loses $0.40 because overtime pushes its cost above the price. The bakery should stop at the point where marginal cost rises above $3. Making 300 ignores the loss on later cupcakes, a big price increase could drive customers away, and cutting to 100 gives up cupcakes that earn a profit.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe marginal analysis techniques and applications

questions.question: When a team member disagrees with the group's plan, the most effective response is to

options.A: refuse to help until the plan changes.
options.B: complain to people outside the team.

questions.explanation: Share concerns and offer alternatives. Effective team members voice disagreements openly and constructively, explaining their concerns and suggesting solutions, which gives the team a chance to improve the plan. Refusing to help damages trust and delays the work, and complaining to outsiders spreads conflict without solving it. Quietly going along may seem polite, but it keeps useful ideas from the team. If the group still chooses the original plan after discussion, a good team member supports the decision and works to make it succeed.

performanceIndicator.text: Participate as a team member

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a social factor affecting global trade:

options.A: Central bank interest rates

questions.explanation: How people prefer to shop. Social factors include customs, lifestyles, values and buying habits, such as whether people prefer to shop online, in large stores or at small local markets. These preferences affect how companies sell and distribute products abroad. Exchange rates and interest rates are economic factors, and tariffs are political or legal factors set by governments. Companies entering a new market study all of these factors, but social factors often determine how products, packaging and sales channels must be adapted.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the impact of cultural and social environments on global trade

questions.question: Theo, 25, keeps all $15,000 of his savings in a checking account that pays no interest. Inflation has averaged 3% a year. The main problem with this approach is that his money

options.A: is taxed at a higher rate.
options.C: is not insured by the government.

questions.explanation: Loses buying power each year. With no interest and 3% inflation, the same $15,000 buys about 3% less each year, so Theo's savings slowly lose buying power. Moving part of it into a high-yield savings account or investments could help it keep up with or beat inflation. His money isn't growing at all, a zero-interest account produces no taxable interest, and checking accounts at insured banks are covered by the FDIC up to its limits. Keeping some money in checking for bills is wise, but long-term savings should earn a return.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need to save and invest

questions.question: Which of the following describes how strong governance processes help managers make better decisions:

options.A: By removing all rules from decisions
options.B: By requiring careful review of risks
options.C: By letting managers ignore shareholder views
options.D: By having the board make every decision

questions.explanation: By requiring careful review of risks. Governance processes, such as risk reviews, board approvals and ethics policies, push managers to think through risks, costs and effects on employees, customers and shareholders before acting, which can prevent costly mistakes. Governance adds structure rather than removing rules, and it protects shareholders' interests instead of ignoring them. Boards set direction and approve major decisions, but day-to-day decisions stay with managers. Well-designed processes match the level of review to the size of the decision so that routine choices aren't slowed down.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the impact of governance processes on decision-making and management functions

questions.question: A company publishes an annual report on its carbon emissions, water use and community programs alongside its financial statements. Investors who care about sustainability mainly use this report to

options.A: compare their environmental impact.

questions.explanation: Compare their environmental impact. Sustainability reports share nonfinancial information about how a company affects the environment and society. Many investors use them to compare companies and to judge long-term risks, such as future environmental rules or damage to the company's reputation. The reports aren't used to calculate taxes, check prices or set credit ratings, which depend on financial data. Some investment funds buy only companies that meet certain sustainability standards, giving companies an incentive to measure and report this information carefully.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss non-traditional uses for financial information (e.g., lean, sustainability reporting, activity-based costing [ABC], six sigma)

questions.question: A manager who studies budget variances should usually give the most attention to

options.A: large or repeated differences.

questions.explanation: Large or repeated differences. Managers have limited time, so they focus on variances that are large or that keep happening, because these are most likely to signal real problems or opportunities. This approach is called management by exception. Investigating every tiny difference wastes time, looking only at favorable variances ignores overspending, and variances from earlier years are less useful for current decisions. Repeated small variances deserve attention too, since they can add up and may show that the budget itself needs to be revised.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the use of variance analysis in managerial accounting

questions.question: A U.S. clothing company plans to sell in a country where most people dress modestly for religious reasons. To succeed there, the company should

options.A: sell its current styles unchanged.

questions.explanation: Adapt designs to local values. Cultural and religious values shape what consumers want to buy and how they respond to marketing. Adapting designs to local expectations of modesty shows respect and makes the products more appealing. Selling current styles unchanged could lead to poor sales or offend customers, lower prices won't fix products people don't want, and U.S. celebrities may not appeal to local buyers. Global brands typically research local culture before entering a market and adjust products, messages and store designs to fit.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the impact of cultural and social environments on global trade

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to change how a public company structures its board of directors:

options.A: A new rule on director independence
options.D: Expansion into a new overseas market

questions.explanation: A new rule on director independence. Stock exchange and regulatory rules often set requirements for boards, such as how many directors must be independent or which committees must exist, so a new independence rule could force the company to add or replace directors. A new office lease, a supplier change and an overseas expansion are operational decisions with no effect on how the board is structured. Ownership changes, company size, industry regulations and investor pressure are among the other factors that commonly reshape governance structures.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the factors that impact governance structures

questions.question: A brokerage firm's compliance software automatically records every phone call between its brokers and clients. The main reason for this is to

options.A: train new brokers in sales techniques.
options.B: shorten the length of client calls.

questions.explanation: Keep records that regulators require. Financial regulators require brokerage firms to keep records of many client communications so that complaints and possible misconduct can be investigated later. Recording calls automatically makes sure no required record is missed. Recordings can be useful for training or for tracking call volume, but those are side benefits rather than the main reason, and recording doesn't shorten calls. Firms must store recordings securely and for a set number of years, since they contain private client information and may be requested in an investigation.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in compliance

questions.question: Dovetail Furniture allocates $30,000 in factory maintenance costs based on machine hours. Last quarter the chair line used 600 machine hours, the table line used 900, and the cabinet line used 1,500. How much maintenance cost is allocated to the table line?
questions.explanation: $9,000. Total machine hours are 600 + 900 + 1,500 = 3,000. The table line used 900 / 3,000 = 30% of the hours, so it is allocated 30% x $30,000 = $9,000. Splitting the cost equally among three lines gives $10,000, $15,000 is the cabinet line's share, and $6,000 is the chair line's share. Allocating by machine hours makes sense here because product lines that run machines longer cause more wear and therefore more maintenance.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of cost allocation

questions.question: Monroe Savings Bank's compliance officer learns that a new federal rule will change how overdraft fees must be disclosed, starting in six months. The bank's current account documents don't meet the new standard. What should the compliance officer do first?

options.A: Stop charging overdraft fees permanently
options.B: Wait until the rule takes effect
options.C: Plan document updates and staff training
options.D: Ask regulators to exempt the bank

questions.explanation: Plan document updates and staff training. A compliance function monitors new laws and makes sure the organization is ready before they take effect. With six months' notice, the officer should plan updates to account documents and customer notices and train employees to explain the change correctly. Waiting until the deadline risks violations and fines. Ending overdraft fees goes beyond what the rule requires and is a business decision, not a compliance step. Exemptions are rare and wouldn't be a sensible first move. Planning early is the heart of effective compliance.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry

questions.question: Which of the following is usually the most logical basis for allocating a building's cleaning costs among departments:

options.A: Square footage used
options.C: Number of employees hired this year

questions.explanation: Square footage used. Cleaning costs rise with the amount of space being cleaned, so square footage is a logical cost driver: departments that use more space are charged more. Hiring, sales revenue and managers' years of service don't determine how much cleaning a department needs. Sales revenue is sometimes used to allocate costs because it is easy to measure, but it can unfairly burden profitable departments. Choosing a basis that reflects what actually causes a cost gives managers a more accurate picture of each department's true cost.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of cost allocation

questions.question: Larchmont Café budgeted $8,000 for food costs in May and spent $7,200. During the same month, several regular customers complained that portion sizes were smaller than usual. What should the manager conclude?

options.A: The food budget was set too high
options.B: The café should cut food costs further
options.C: The savings may reflect a quality problem

questions.explanation: The savings may reflect a quality problem. The café spent $800 less than planned, a favorable variance, but the complaints suggest the savings came from smaller portions. Managers investigate favorable variances too, because savings that hurt quality can cost more in lost customers than they save. Cutting costs further could make the problem worse, any significant variance deserves an explanation, and nothing shows the budget itself was too high. The manager should check whether kitchen staff changed portion sizes and restore the standard if they did.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the use of variance analysis in managerial accounting

questions.question: Marginal revenue is the

options.A: revenue from selling one more unit.
options.B: revenue from the first unit sold.
options.C: revenue left after paying all costs.
options.D: total revenue earned in a year.

questions.explanation: Revenue from selling one more unit. Marginal revenue measures how much total revenue increases when one more unit is sold. Businesses compare it with marginal cost, the extra cost of producing that unit, to find the most profitable level of output. Total yearly revenue includes every unit sold, revenue left after costs is profit, and the first unit's revenue is only one data point. As long as marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost, producing and selling more adds to profit; once it falls below, extra units reduce profit.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe marginal analysis techniques and applications

questions.question: After a client meeting, Andre's manager tells him that he interrupted the client several times. Andre feels embarrassed. Which response would best help him grow?

options.A: Explain that the client spoke slowly
options.B: Thank his manager and practice listening
options.C: Ignore the comment and move on

questions.explanation: Thank his manager and practice listening. Accepting feedback calmly, even when it's uncomfortable, and turning it into action is how people improve. Andre could thank his manager, ask for tips and practice letting clients finish before responding. Blaming the client avoids responsibility, ignoring the comment means the habit continues, and staying silent in future meetings overcorrects and keeps him from contributing. Following up with the manager after the next meeting to ask whether he improved also shows maturity and builds trust.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of feedback for personal growth

questions.question: In a well-governed company, the audit committee is usually made up of

options.A: the company's external auditors.

questions.explanation: Independent board members. An audit committee is a group of independent directors who oversee financial reporting, internal controls and the work of internal and external auditors. Independence matters because members must be willing to question management. Senior executives prepare the financial statements, so they can't oversee their own work. Customers have no governance role, and external auditors report to the committee rather than serving on it. Stock exchanges generally require public companies to have audit committees of independent directors, including at least one financial expert.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the components of a well-governed company (e.g., board of directors, reporting, transparency, internal and external audit functions)

questions.question: Sunfield Insurance stores each customer's mailing address in five different systems, and the addresses often don't match. Better information management would

options.A: add a sixth system to check addresses.
options.B: let each department keep its own list.

questions.explanation: Keep one trusted customer record. When the same information is stored in several places, updates made in one system may never reach the others, creating conflicting records. Information management solves this by keeping one trusted source that other systems draw from. Adding another system makes the problem worse, separate department lists create even more inconsistency, and erasing addresses would leave the company unable to send required documents. Accurate customer data matters in insurance because a wrong address can mean missed bills, lapsed policies and unhappy customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of information management

questions.question: While scanning its business environment, an insurance company learns that severe storms in its region have become much more frequent over the past decade. How might it best use this information?

options.A: Adjust coverage and pricing for the higher risk
options.B: Stop selling all insurance in the region
options.C: Lower premiums to attract new customers
options.D: Ignore the trend because weather is uncontrollable

questions.explanation: Adjust coverage and pricing for the higher risk. More frequent storms mean more claims, so the insurer may need to adjust prices, encourage storm-resistant building features or buy reinsurance to manage the risk. Environmental scanning is valuable precisely because it reveals trends a business can't control but must prepare for. Leaving the region entirely is an extreme reaction, ignoring the trend could lead to large losses, and cutting premiums would make the problem worse. Many insurers also offer discounts to customers who reduce storm risk, such as by reinforcing roofs.

performanceIndicator.text: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information

questions.question: Which of the following is a variable cost for a pizza restaurant:

options.A: Cheese

questions.explanation: Cheese. Variable costs change with the amount produced or sold: the more pizzas the restaurant makes, the more cheese it buys. Rent, a salaried manager's pay and insurance premiums stay the same each month whether the restaurant sells 500 pizzas or 5,000, so they are fixed costs. Knowing which costs are variable helps the owner set prices and estimate how much profit each extra pizza adds. When sales rise, variable costs rise with them, while fixed costs are spread over more pizzas.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of costs used in managerial accounting (e.g., direct cost, indirect cost, sunk cost, differential cost, etc.)

questions.question: The two owners of a fast-growing software partnership want to raise money from outside investors and protect their personal assets. Why might they convert the business into a corporation?

options.A: To make each owner liable for all debts
options.C: To sell shares and limit liability
options.D: To keep all profits out of taxable income

questions.explanation: To sell shares and limit liability. A corporation can sell shares to investors, which makes it easier to raise large amounts of money for growth, and it protects owners' personal assets from business debts. Partners in a general partnership are already personally liable, so converting would reduce that risk rather than create it. Corporations face more filing requirements, not fewer, and their profits are still taxed. The trade-offs include more paperwork and regulation and, for some corporations, taxes on both company profits and shareholder dividends.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of business ownership

questions.question: An index fund is an investment that

options.A: is sold only to large institutions.

questions.explanation: Tracks a market index. An index fund holds the stocks or bonds in a market index, such as the S&P 500, so its performance closely follows that index. Because managers don't have to research and pick individual investments, index funds usually charge low fees and offer broad diversification. They don't guarantee returns, they hold many companies rather than one, and individual investors can easily buy them through brokerage and retirement accounts. Many financial advisors recommend index funds for long-term goals such as retirement.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of investments

questions.question: A business owned by two or more people who share its profits and are each personally responsible for its debts is a

options.A: sole proprietorship.

questions.explanation: General partnership. In a general partnership, the partners share ownership, decision making and profits, and each partner can be personally liable for the business's debts, even debts created by another partner. A corporation and a limited liability company protect owners' personal assets from business debts, and a sole proprietorship has only one owner. Partners usually sign a partnership agreement that explains how profits, duties and disagreements will be handled, which helps prevent conflicts if the business grows or a partner leaves.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of business ownership

questions.question: Tavola Restaurant Group has been owned and run by one family for 30 years. To fund its expansion into three new states, it recently sold a 40% stake to a private equity firm. Until now, the family's CEO has also chaired a three-person board made up of family members, and major decisions were often made informally over dinner. How is the sale most likely to affect the company's governance?

options.A: The investor will likely gain board seats
options.C: The family will gain more control
options.D: Board meetings will no longer be needed

questions.explanation: The investor will likely gain board seats. Large investors want a say in how their money is used, so they usually receive seats on the board and often add new reporting and approval requirements. The family will now share control rather than gaining more of it. Board meetings will likely become more formal and frequent, not unnecessary, and governance rules continue to apply. A change in ownership is one of the most common reasons governance structures change, especially when a family business takes on outside investors for the first time.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the factors that impact governance structures

questions.question: Activity-based costing may show that a product with many small special orders costs more than traditional costing suggested, because the product

options.A: sells at a lower retail price.

questions.explanation: Uses more setups and handling. Activity-based costing assigns overhead based on the activities each product actually uses, such as machine setups, inspections and order handling. A product with many small special orders requires more of these activities, so ABC assigns it more overhead than a method that spreads overhead evenly by labor hours. Cheaper materials and a lower price don't raise overhead, and fewer labor hours would actually lower its share under traditional costing. ABC helps managers find products that look profitable but actually lose money.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss non-traditional uses for financial information (e.g., lean, sustainability reporting, activity-based costing [ABC], six sigma)

questions.question: Strong corporate governance helps a company attract investors mainly because it

options.A: lowers the risk of mismanagement.
options.B: removes the need for financial reports.
options.C: guarantees that the stock price will rise.

questions.explanation: Lowers the risk of mismanagement. Investors want confidence that a company is run honestly and in shareholders' interests. Good governance, with independent directors, clear policies and transparent reporting, lowers the chance that managers will waste money, take reckless risks or hide problems. It can't guarantee a rising stock price, it depends on accurate financial reports rather than replacing them, and it increases oversight of executives instead of removing it. Studies have found that investors often pay more for shares of well-governed companies because they see them as less risky.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of corporate governance in business

questions.question: A company spent $50,000 last year researching a product it has now decided not to launch. When choosing its next project, managers should treat the $50,000 as a

options.A: sunk cost.

questions.explanation: Sunk cost. Money already spent that can't be recovered is a sunk cost. Because it won't change no matter what the company decides, it shouldn't influence future choices, even though managers sometimes feel they must keep going to "get their money back." A variable cost changes with output, an opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up, and a marginal cost is the cost of producing one more unit. Good decisions compare only future costs and benefits.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of costs used in managerial accounting (e.g., direct cost, indirect cost, sunk cost, differential cost, etc.)

questions.question: A finance team is preparing a report due Friday. On Wednesday, Lila finishes her section early, while two teammates are behind on theirs. Which action best shows that she is an effective team member?

options.A: Offer to help teammates who are behind
options.C: Use the extra time to polish her section
options.D: Tell the manager who is behind

questions.explanation: Offer to help teammates who are behind. Effective team members care about the team's success, not just their own tasks. Offering help to teammates who are behind increases the chance that the report is finished well and on time. Starting next month's work or polishing her own section ignores the team's immediate need, and reporting teammates to the manager before offering help may damage trust. Teams whose members support one another usually produce better work, and the habit often leads others to help Lila when she falls behind.

performanceIndicator.text: Participate as a team member

questions.question: Which of the following is the main reason to keep an emergency fund in a savings account rather than in stocks:

options.A: Stocks can't be sold during emergencies
options.C: It can be withdrawn quickly without losses
options.D: Savings accounts earn more than stocks

questions.explanation: It can be withdrawn quickly without losses. An emergency fund must be available immediately for unexpected costs, such as car repairs or a job loss. A savings account lets people withdraw money quickly without the risk of having to sell stocks at a loss during a market drop. Stocks often grow more over the long run, so savings accounts usually earn less, not more. Stocks can be sold at any time, but their price may be low just when the money is needed. Many advisors suggest saving three to six months of expenses.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the need to save and invest

questions.question: A bank's compliance department reviews new advertisements before they run mainly to make sure the ads

options.A: cost less than last year's ads.

questions.explanation: Follow consumer protection rules. Financial advertising is regulated, so ads must describe rates, fees and terms accurately and include required disclosures. Compliance staff review ads before they run to catch misleading claims or missing information, which protects customers and keeps the bank out of legal trouble. Brand standards, audience reach and advertising costs matter to the marketing department, but they aren't legal requirements and aren't the reason compliance reviews ads. Fixing a problem before publication is far cheaper than paying fines or correcting an ad after regulators or customers complain.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry

questions.question: Sofia earns $600 a month from her part-time job. She wants to have $1,500 for a trip in 10 months and has already saved $300. What percentage of her monthly income must she save to reach her goal?
questions.explanation: 20%. Sofia needs $1,500 - $300 = $1,200 more. Over 10 months, that is $1,200 / 10 = $120 per month, and $120 / $600 = 0.20, or 20% of her income. An answer of 25% comes from ignoring the $300 she already saved ($1,500 / 10 = $150, which is 25% of $600). 10% halves the needed amount, and 50% treats the $300 as a monthly figure. Turning a goal into a monthly amount and a percentage of income helps her build it into her budget.

performanceIndicator.text: Set financial goals

questions.question: On a statement of changes in equity, retained earnings increase when the company

options.A: reports a net loss for the year.
options.B: buys back some of its own shares.
options.D: earns a net profit that it keeps.

questions.explanation: Earns a net profit that it keeps. Retained earnings are the profits a company has kept over time instead of paying them out. Net income that isn't paid as dividends adds to retained earnings, while dividends and net losses reduce them. Buying back shares lowers total equity, but it is usually recorded in a separate equity account rather than as an increase in retained earnings. Investors watch retained earnings because they show how much profit the company has reinvested in its operations, such as new equipment, research or expansion.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of statements of changes in equity

questions.question: A student wants to set a financial goal she can actually track. Which of the following goals would work best:

options.A: Become rich someday
options.C: Pay off $1,200 of card debt by June
options.D: Save as much money as I possibly can

questions.explanation: Pay off $1,200 of card debt by June. Effective financial goals are specific, measurable and time-bound. Paying off $1,200 by June states the amount and the deadline, so the person can work out a monthly payment and track progress. "Spend less money soon," "become rich someday" and "save as much as I can" are vague goals that are hard to measure and easy to abandon. Writing a goal this way also makes it easier to adjust a budget to support it, such as by cutting a specific expense.

performanceIndicator.text: Set financial goals

questions.question: A bank's database designer changes the "loan type" field from free text to a dropdown list of five options. The main benefit of this design is

options.A: a smaller database file on the server.

questions.explanation: More consistent, accurate data. Dropdown lists prevent spelling errors and inconsistent entries, such as "auto," "car loan" and "vehicle" all describing the same thing. Consistent data makes searches and reports accurate, which helps managers analyze the loan portfolio correctly. The change doesn't speed up loan approvals, meaningfully shrink the database or affect password protection. Data validation tools like dropdowns, required fields and format checks are basic parts of good database design, because decisions are only as good as the data behind them.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate advanced database applications

questions.question: Briarwood Foods began the year with retained earnings of $200,000. It earned $90,000 in net income and paid $40,000 in dividends. What were its retained earnings at the end of the year?
questions.explanation: $250,000. Ending retained earnings equal beginning retained earnings plus net income minus dividends: $200,000 + $90,000 - $40,000 = $250,000. Adding the dividends instead of subtracting them gives $330,000. Leaving out the dividends gives $290,000, and $160,000 subtracts the dividends but forgets to add net income. This calculation appears on the statement of changes in equity and shows how much of the year's profit the company chose to keep and reinvest in the business rather than pay to its owners.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of statements of changes in equity

questions.question: Which action by an employee best supports a company's governance objectives:

options.A: Sharing board decisions with friends
options.C: Approving his or her own expenses
options.D: Ignoring a known conflict of interest

questions.explanation: Completing compliance training on time. Governance depends on every employee following policies and understanding his or her responsibilities. Completing required compliance training helps employees recognize and avoid problems such as conflicts of interest, improper gifts and unauthorized disclosures. Sharing confidential board decisions, ignoring a conflict of interest and approving one's own expenses all undermine governance and may violate company policy or the law. Many companies track training completion because regulators expect employees to know the rules that apply to their jobs.

performanceIndicator.text: Ascertain employee's role in achieving governance objectives

questions.question: Brightside Candles planned to make 1,000 candles using $2 of wax each, for a wax budget of $2,000. It actually made 1,200 candles and spent $2,500 on wax. Using a flexible budget, what is the wax variance?

options.A: $500 unfavorable

questions.explanation: $100 unfavorable. A flexible budget adjusts to actual production: 1,200 candles x $2 = $2,400 of wax should have been used. Actual spending was $2,500, or $100 more than the flexible budget, so the variance is $100 unfavorable. Comparing with the original $2,000 budget gives $500 unfavorable, which unfairly blames the factory for making more candles. Calling it $100 favorable reverses the direction, and $400 favorable compares the flexible budget with the original budget. Flexible budgets separate the effect of higher output from spending efficiency.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of cost accounting budgets

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a corporate governance practice:

options.A: Opening a new regional office
options.B: Launching a new national product line

questions.explanation: Holding an annual shareholders' meeting. Corporate governance covers how a company is directed and controlled, including how shareholders, the board and managers interact. An annual shareholders' meeting lets owners vote on directors and major issues and question leaders, which keeps management accountable. Launching products, negotiating with suppliers and opening offices are business decisions that managers make; they don't concern who controls the company or how leaders are held responsible. Public companies are required by law to hold shareholder meetings and send owners information before each vote.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of corporate governance in business

questions.question: Which of the following best describes what effective information management does for a business:

options.A: Keeping all information hidden from employees
options.B: Collecting as much data as possible
options.D: Getting the right information to the right people

questions.explanation: Getting the right information to the right people. Information management makes sure employees can find accurate, up-to-date information when they need it, while protecting sensitive data from people who shouldn't see it. Hiding everything from employees would keep them from doing their jobs. Collecting as much data as possible without a purpose wastes storage and creates privacy risks, and paper-only storage is slow to search and easy to lose. Good information management balances access, accuracy and security, and it decides how long each type of record should be kept.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of information management

questions.question: An environmental scan helps a financial services business by

options.A: reviewing the company's own policies.

questions.explanation: Finding outside trends and threats. An environmental scan studies external factors, such as economic trends, technology, laws, competitors and social changes, that could create opportunities or threats. A bank might notice that more customers want mobile banking or that a new competitor is entering the area. Employee satisfaction, daily cash and internal policies are internal matters, which a business reviews through its own records and surveys rather than an environmental scan. Regular scanning helps businesses plan ahead rather than simply react to surprises.

performanceIndicator.text: Conduct an environmental scan to obtain business information

questions.question: Which of the following investments is most likely to lose a large share of its value:

options.A: Shares of a startup

questions.explanation: Shares of a startup. Shares of a new startup can rise sharply if the company succeeds but can also lose most or all of their value if it fails, so they carry high risk. Insured savings accounts and bank certificates of deposit are protected up to FDIC limits, and short-term Treasury bills are backed by the U.S. government, making them among the safest investments. Higher potential returns usually come with higher risk, which is why investors spread money across different types of investments.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of investments

questions.question: A company's governance policy requires board approval for any loan over $1 million. As a result, managers must

options.A: report all loans after the fact.

questions.explanation: Get approval before large borrowing. Governance policies set limits on management's authority to protect the company from risky decisions. Managers can still borrow, but loans above $1 million need board approval in advance, which adds a review step and accountability. The policy doesn't ban borrowing, allow large loans to be reported only after they happen, or let departments borrow without limits. Clear approval thresholds help managers know which decisions they can make on their own and which require oversight from the board.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the impact of governance processes on decision-making and management functions

questions.question: Seven of the nine directors on Calloway Industries' board are current or former company executives. Which of the following explains why investors might see this as a governance weakness:

options.A: Nine directors is too many to make decisions
options.B: The board may not oversee management independently

questions.explanation: The board may not oversee management independently. Directors are supposed to oversee management on behalf of shareholders. When most board members are current or former executives, they may hesitate to challenge decisions made by people they worked with, which weakens independent oversight. Nine directors is a common board size, former executives usually know the industry well, and directors don't have to be shareholders. Governance guidelines and stock exchange rules generally call for a majority of independent directors so that the board can judge management objectively.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the components of a well-governed company (e.g., board of directors, reporting, transparency, internal and external audit functions)

questions.question: Unlike financial accounting reports, managerial accounting reports are usually prepared

options.A: in formats set by regulators.
options.B: once a year for the public.

questions.explanation: Whenever managers need them. Managerial accounting serves decision makers inside the company, so reports can be produced weekly, daily or whenever a decision requires them, in whatever format is most useful. Financial accounting produces standardized statements, usually quarterly and annually, for outside users such as investors and lenders. Formats set by regulators and reports for tax authorities belong to financial and tax accounting. This flexibility lets managers track things like the cost of each product line, the profit of each store or the results of a single promotion.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of managerial accounting

questions.question: The owner of Highline Bikes wants to decide whether to keep selling a line of children's bikes. She asks her accountant for a report showing the sales, costs and profit of each product line for the last six months. This request is an example of

options.A: tax accounting.

questions.explanation: Managerial accounting. Managerial accounting provides internal reports designed to help managers make decisions, such as which products to keep, expand or drop, and a product-line profit report is a classic example. External auditing is an independent review of financial statements for outside users. Tax accounting prepares returns and plans for taxes, and financial reporting produces standardized statements for investors and lenders. Because this report is for the owner's own decision, it can be organized however is most useful to her rather than following official reporting rules.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of managerial accounting

questions.question: In a database, a primary key is a field that

options.A: links the database to the internet.
options.C: holds the largest value in a table.

questions.explanation: Uniquely identifies every record. A primary key, such as a customer ID or account number, gives every record a unique value so the database can find, sort and link records accurately. No two records can share the same primary key. Passwords are stored and protected separately, the largest value in a table is just data, and internet connections are handled by networks rather than by fields. Primary keys are also what allow related tables, such as customers and their orders, to be joined correctly.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate advanced database applications

questions.question: A flexible budget is useful to a manufacturer because it

options.A: stays the same at every output level.

questions.explanation: Adjusts costs to actual output. A flexible budget recalculates what costs should have been at the level of production actually achieved. If a factory produced more units than planned, it naturally used more materials, so comparing actual costs with a flexible budget gives a fair picture of efficiency. A static budget is the one that stays the same regardless of output, which can make variances misleading. Flexible budgets still require tracking actual costs, and they don't affect supplier prices, which are set through purchasing agreements.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of cost accounting budgets

questions.question: Feedback is most useful for personal growth when it is

options.A: focused on personality.

questions.explanation: Specific. Specific feedback, such as "your report's charts were hard to read," tells a person exactly what to change, which makes improvement possible. Feedback given only once a year comes too late to fix many problems, comments about personality can feel like personal attacks rather than guidance, and sharing criticism publicly can embarrass people and make them defensive. People who want to grow can ask for specific examples when the feedback they receive is general, and can ask for feedback more often than formal reviews provide it.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of feedback for personal growth

questions.question: Isabel, a purchasing agent at Northgate Supply, is asked to choose a new packaging supplier. One of the five bidders is owned by her cousin, and its bid appears to be the lowest. According to good governance practices, what should she do?

options.A: Pick her cousin's company quietly
options.B: Disclose the relationship and step aside
options.C: Ask her cousin to lower the price further
options.D: Reject her cousin's bid without explanation

questions.explanation: Disclose the relationship and step aside. A family relationship with a bidder is a conflict of interest, even if the cousin's company really offers the best price. Disclosing the relationship and letting someone else make the decision protects the fairness of the process and Isabel's reputation. Choosing the cousin without comment hides the conflict, rejecting the bid without explanation could unfairly cost the company a good deal, and asking for a better price privately gives the cousin an unfair advantage. Most companies require employees to report conflicts so they can be managed openly.

performanceIndicator.text: Ascertain employee's role in achieving governance objectives
